chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Saʿīd Ibn ʿUqdah, from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf ibn Ibrāhīm, from Maḥmūd ibn Maymūn, from Jaʿfar ibn Suwayd ibn Jaʿfar ibn Kilāb, who said:

I heard Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام saying: “The grave of a woman is covered with a cloth, while the grave of a man is not covered. And a cloth had been stretched over the grave of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh while the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was present and did not disapprove of that.”

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man; contrasted with the ruling for the woman
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman; indicating the specific legal distinction mentioned
key_terms.ثَوْبٌ: a cloth used to cover or stretch over the grave
key_terms.قَبْرُ: grave; the burial place being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.لَمْ يُنْكِرْ: he did not object or disapprove

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to cover a grave with a cloth during burial in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a ruling concerning covering the grave during burial, distinguishing between the grave of a woman and that of a man. It also cites the incident of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh as a precedent witnessed by the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, indicating permissibility in that case.
